questionText:
Read the following case study on data structures in Python and answer the questions that follow:

Rohan is designing a document editing application in Python. To implement the 'Undo' and 'Redo' operations, he utilizes a Stack data structure based on the Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) principle. He implements the stack using a standard Python list named undo_stack = []. Whenever the user performs an edit action (such as typing text or deleting a character), a descriptor of that action is pushed onto undo_stack using the append() method. When the user clicks 'Undo', the application checks if the stack is empty. If undo_stack is empty (i.e., len(undo_stack) == 0), the function outputs 'Underflow: Nothing to Undo'. Otherwise, it removes and retrieves the topmost operation using undo_stack.pop(), reversing the action and pushing it onto redo_stack.

Question: How can Rohan inspect the topmost action without removing it from undo_stack?

questionText:
Match the search concept in List I with its algorithmic property in List II:

List I:
(A) Linear Search Best Case
(B) Linear Search Worst Case
(C) Binary Search Best Case
(D) Binary Search Worst Case

List II:
(I) O(1) (target element found at the very first index position 0)
(II) O(n) (target element at the last index or absent entirely)
(III) O(1) (target element located at the exact initial midpoint)
(IV) O(log n) (search space repeatedly halved until low > high)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV

options.text: A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Linear best is O(1) at index 0, worst O(n); Binary best is O(1) at mid, worst O(log n).
Hence Option D is correct.
Hence, option (A) is the correct match.

questionText:
Arrange the sequential execution steps of Binary Search searching for target 'key' in sorted list L with bounds low and high:
(A) Initialize low = 0 and high = len(L) - 1
(B) While low <= high, compute midpoint index mid = (low + high) // 2
(C) If L[mid] == key, return mid (successful search termination)
(D) If L[mid] < key set low = mid + 1; else set high = mid - 1; if loop ends return -1

Choose the correct chronological/logical sequence from the options given below:

options.text: B, A, C, D
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: A, B, C, D
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.

options.text: A, C, B, D
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: D, B, C, A
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Binary search: set bounds -> compute mid -> test equality -> adjust bounds based on magnitude -> return -1 if exhausted.
Hence Option A is correct.
Hence, option (B) is correct.
